answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each identity to post a decaying proof-of-history bond: the harder it is to fabricate a credible past, the higher the entry cost. Think of a tide that resets every epoch, so a fresh identity must rebuild reputation from zero and cannot inherit an old record. Reputation is bound to the identity's stake, which must be forfeited on misbehavior, and each new identity emerges from a narrow karst channel — one expensive, auditable birth per head. Violet flags mark anomalous clusters, so duplicates become visible rather than profitable.
